identity.title: exoALMA. X. Channel Maps Reveal Complex <SUP>12</SUP>CO Abundance Distributions and a Variety of Kinematic Structures with Evidence for Embedded Planets

paper_type_evidence.quote: The remarkable sensitivity of the exoALMA Large Program (cite: Teague_exoALMA) enables us to map molecular line emission from protoplanetary disks with unprecedented detail.

targets.name: 15 exoALMA disks (MWC 758, HD 135344B, CQ Tau, J1604, AA Tau, SY Cha, J1842, J1615, LkCa 15, HD 143006, J1852, DM Tau, HD 34282, V4046 Sgr, PDS 66)

question.value: What kinematic substructures and CO abundance distributions appear in individual 12CO J=3-2 channel maps of the 15 exoALMA disks, and are they consistent with embedded planets?

evidence.quote: In this paper, we extend the analysis to individual channel maps, which provide a complementary approach by isolating specific velocity channels across the emission line profiles.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.01123.L.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 12CO J=3-2 cubes; velocity resolution ≈26 m/s; binned 28 to 200 m/s

evidence.quote: With a velocity resolution of $\approx 26\mathrm{m\,s}^{-1}$ and spatial resolution of $\approx 0.1\ensuremath{''}$
We analyze the $^{12}$CO $J=3-2$ data cubes of the disks in the exoALMA program.

angular_resolution.value: ≈0.1'' native; inspected 0.1'' to 0.3''; 0.25'' for faint emission

evidence.quote: We inspected the $^{12}$CO $J=3-2$ exoALMA data cubes at various spatial ($0.1\ensuremath{''}$ to $0.3\ensuremath{''}$) and spectral (28 to 200 m/s) resolutions

what.value: Gardner et al. higher-resolution LkCa 15 imaging with extra velocity kink

evidence.quote: (cite: Gardner_exoALMA) detected an additional velocity kink at the systemic velocity at a separation of $\lesssim 0.1\ensuremath{''}$

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: phantom SPH + mcfost models with a planet of 1, 2, 5 or 10 MJup per disk

evidence.quote: we embedded a single planet at the projected location of the detected primary kinks with an initial mass of 1, 2, 5, or 10 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$

continuum_subtraction.value: Cubes imaged without continuum subtraction; checked that kinematic deviations also appear in continuum-subtracted maps

evidence.quote: we imaged all the channel maps without continuum subtraction, and checked that the detected kinematic deviations are also present in the corresponding continuum-subtracted maps.

what.value: Standard exoALMA imaging procedure, with additional weighting schemes and spectral binning

evidence.quote: we also reimaged the visibilities using the standard exoALMA imaging procedure (cite: Loomis_exoALMA)

what.value: Regularized maximum likelihood reimaging for selected disks

evidence.quote: reimaged using regularized maximum likelihood imaging instead of CLEAN (cite: Zawadzki_exoALMA)

what.value: CO abundance prescription for freeze-out, photodissociation and photodesorption

evidence.quote: We set the CO abundance following the prescription in Appendix B of (cite: Pinte2018a)

unstated_but_needed: Weighting schemes (robust, taper) and exact channel binning for each disk's reimaged cubes
Which channels are shown for each disk
Exact dynamite fitting setup and uncertainties
Beam and noise for the Figure 6 cubes
Number of mcfost photons and grid setup

analysis_steps.goal: Reimage cubes and inspect channel maps

method.value: Reimaged exoALMA visibilities at several resolutions and binnings without continuum subtraction, and checked against continuum-subtracted maps and regularized maximum likelihood imaging

evidence.quote: we imaged all the channel maps without continuum subtraction, and checked that the detected kinematic deviations are also present in the corresponding continuum-subtracted maps.

validation.value: Compared CLEAN, continuum-subtracted and regularized maximum likelihood images

evidence.quote: confirming that the detections presented here are not artifacts of the imaging process.

analysis_steps.goal: Overlay Keplerian isovelocity curves and classify structures

method.value: Used dynamite to extract geometry, stellar mass and emission-layer height, then visually classified deviations

evidence.quote: We used the code dynamite (cite: Pinte2018a) to extract the disk’s geometric parameters (outer radius, inclination, position angle (PA), and systemic velocity, and stellar masses)
assuming the disks are in Keplerian rotation

validation.value: Parameters consistent with discminer values and emission surfaces from Galloway et al.

evidence.quote: We verified that all those parameters are consistent with the values derived with discminer by (cite: Izquierdo_exoALMA)

method.value: 3D gas-only SPH with phantom, 10^6 particles, 20 orbits, then each particle split into 13 and evolved 2 more orbits

evidence.quote: We used $10^6$ particles and evolved the system for 20 planet orbits

key_parameters.value: alpha_av = 0.2; inner radius 5 au; H/R=0.1 at 50 au; gamma=0.8; accretion radius 0.125 Hill radius

evidence.quote: we set the shock viscosity to $\alpha_{\rm av} = 0.2$

assumptions.value: Vertically isothermal; self-gravity neglected; disk mass 5e-3 Msun

evidence.quote: We neglect self-gravity and use a disk mass of $5 \times 10^{-3} \, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ for all disks

fitting.value: No formal fit; restricted grid of planet masses

evidence.quote: Our aim is not to develop a detailed model for each source; instead, we test, through a restricted exploration of the parameter space, whether a single planet can reasonably explain the observed channel maps.

validation.value: phantom+mcfost benchmarked by Bae et al.

evidence.quote: The combination of phantom and mcfost was benchmarked and validated by (cite: Bae_exoALMA).

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer synthetic CO channel maps

method.value: mcfost for dust temperature and CO maps with Voronoi cells matched to SPH particles; Tgas=Tdust, LTE

evidence.quote: We postprocessed the models with the radiative transfer code mcfost (cite: Pinte2006; Pinte2009) to compute the dust temperature structure and CO maps

key_parameters.value: 12CO abundance 1e-4 relative to H in warm layer; depleted below 20 K by a variable factor

evidence.quote: Below 20 K, we deplete this abundance by a factor that we allow to vary

assumptions.value: Astrosilicate grains, dn ∝ a^-3.5 da, 0.03-1000 micron, gas-to-dust 100; zero turbulent velocity; 1 Myr isochrones

evidence.quote: a uniform gas-to-dust ratio of 100

validation.value: Visual comparison of kink shape and amplitude with data

evidence.quote: The planet model matches the observations well for LkCa 15, J1615, and J1842, in terms of both shape and amplitude of the kink.

analysis_steps.goal: Compare models to data and constrain planet mass and CO depletion

method.value: Visual comparison of the channel with the most visible kink; compared depletion factors in Fig. 8

evidence.quote: For each source, we compare the channel where the velocity kink is most visible to our synthetic models.
We do not attempt to precisely match the brightness of the emitting upper and lower surfaces or the midplane.

validation.value: Depletion varied for a single hydrodynamical model only; range indicative

evidence.quote: We note that this range is only indicative, as we varied the freeze-out fraction for a single hydrodynamical model
casa (cite: casa)
casa_cube (cite: casa_cube)
We used the code dynamite (cite: Pinte2018a)
We performed 3D gas-only simulations with the Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) code phantom (cite: Price2018).
We postprocessed the models with the radiative transfer code mcfost
pymcfost (cite: pymcfost)

results_numeric.quantity: Disks with velocity deviations in channel maps

evidence.quote: We visually detect velocity deviations in $^{12}$CO channel maps in 13 of the 15 exoALMA objects.
suggests planets with orbital radii between 80 and 310 au and masses between 1 and 5 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$.

results_numeric.quantity: Planet masses (AA Tau, J1615, LkCa 15 / SY Cha / J1842)

evidence.quote: best reproduced with a planet mass of 2 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$ for LkCa 15, AA Tau, and J1615, 5 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$ for SY Cha, and 1 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$ for J1842.
with a depletion factor of $\approx 10^{-3}$ – $10^{-2}$ compared to the warm molecular layer.

results_numeric.quantity: Lower limit on planet mass detectable by kinematics

evidence.quote: currently sets the lower limit for the kinematic detection of planets to $\approx$ 1 M$_\mathrm{Jup}$.

findings_qualitative.value: Midplane 12CO emission is detected between surfaces in 7 disks with favorable inclination, and CO desorption is seen in outer regions

evidence.quote: The vertical CO snowline is clearly detected in seven disks where the upper and lower emission surfaces are well separated.

claims.hypothesis: Kinematic kinks in exoALMA disks are caused by embedded planets
claims.experiment: phantom+mcfost single-planet models compared to channel maps
claims.result: Planets of 1-5 MJup at 80-310 au reproduce the kinks in several disks; 10 MJup too strong
claims.finding: Six disks show signatures consistent with planet wakes, though models are imperfect

evidence.quote: Kinematic signatures observed in six disks point toward the presence of embedded planets.

claims.hypothesis: CO is not fully frozen out in the midplane
claims.experiment: Examined emission between upper and lower surfaces and compared with models of varied depletion
claims.result: Non-zero midplane emission; depletion 1e-3 to 1e-2 fits better than full or no freeze-out

evidence.quote: models with a depletion factor between $10^{-3}$ and $10^{-2}$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Alternatives to planets (MRI, GI, VSI, buoyancy spirals, vertical thermal structure) are discussed but not tested

evidence.quote: Other physical processes can also produce deviations from Keplerian rotation, including magneto-rotational instability (MRI), GI, and vertical shear instability
Our classification is subjective, and some sources clearly exhibit multiple types of substructures.

limitations_admitted.value: Vertically isothermal assumption is a major limitation

evidence.quote: One major limitation of our models is the assumption of a vertically isothermal profile in phantom.

referee_caveats_inferred: Planet detection is by visual comparison with no quantitative fit or uncertainty
Planet masses degenerate with other kinematic structures and a single-planet model
Depletion constraint from a single hydrodynamical model

data_public_as_stated.value: Models are public; ALMA data are from an ALMA Large Program

evidence.quote: The phantom and mcfost models are available in (cite: DVN/H5QUQT_2025).

code_released.value: phantom and mcfost models in Harvard Dataverse

evidence.quote: The phantom and mcfost models are available in (cite: DVN/H5QUQT_2025).

missing_for_reproduction: Imaging parameters for each reimaged cube
Full simulation inputs beyond the released models
reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Hundreds of GB for 15 disks' calibrated exoALMA cubes; simulations are additional compute
reproducibility.score_reason: Data and models are available, but classification and model comparison are qualitative and imaging details are inherited.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main results are qualitative visual classifications and a restricted model comparison, not a numeric recipe.
